links.outcome: Proportion of inappropriate LLM responses found via adversarial red teaming with clinicians and students
links.effect: Of 376 unique prompts (1504 responses), 20.1% were inappropriate (GPT-3.5: 25.8%; GPT-4.0: 16%; GPT-4.0 with Internet: 17.8%); GPT-4o 20.4% inappropriate.
links.quote: Of 376 unique prompts (1504 responses), 20.1% were inappropriate (GPT-3.5: 25.8%; GPT-4.0: 16%; GPT-4.0 with Internet: 17.8%).

links.outcome: Responses appropriate in older model that became inappropriate in updated models
links.effect: 21.5% of responses appropriate with GPT-3.5 were inappropriate in updated models.
links.quote: 21.5% of responses appropriate with GPT-3.5 were inappropriate in updated models.

screen.reason: The study directly evaluates clinical red teaming (adversarial stress-testing by multidisciplinary clinical teams) as a deployment evaluation and safety safeguard for large language models.
